newsitem.title: DENMARK: Phoenix to mull takeover bids at meeting.
newsitem.headline: Phoenix to mull takeover bids at meeting.

text.p: Danish roadbuilder Phoenix Contractors on Tuesday said it was unable to completely recommend any of three takeover bids and summoned shareholders to an extraordinary meeting later in the month to discuss the situation.
Construction and chemicals group Superfos A/S offered last Thursday to pay 700 crowns per share for Phoenix A-shares, and 620 crowns for the most-traded C-share.

The offer trumped an earlier bid by Norway's Rieber and Son but later on the same day was outdone by small provincial Danish building contractor Marius Pedersen which offered 710 crowns per A-share and 625 crowns per C-share.
In a statement the Phoenix board pointed to the Rieber offer as being best for the company's continued independence and future development but said the Norwegian firm's cash offer was too low.
"The job situation and further development of the firm in its present location would be safest in the hands of both Rieber and Pedersen," Phoenix said.
"The two companies would in the board's opinion ensure that Phoenix survives as an independent concern," it said.
It said that the Superfos takeover offer would imply a greater integration of Phoenix activities with that company and thus failed to satisfy its requirements.

"Rieber has the strongest financial basis..but its offer is the lowest of the three. The price difference is too great to outweigh the board's otherwise positive assessment of Rieber and therefore it cannot recommend the bid," it said.
Phoenix summoned shareholders to an extraordinary meeting in Vejen, its west Denmark base, on February 21 to discuss the situation.

The Copenhagen bourse last week put Superfos, Phoenix and Pedersen on its list of shares marked for special observation, standard procedure when a share is more than usually active due to special circumstances.
Danish institutional investors have told Reuters that Superfos, one of the top-20 companies listed on the Copenhagen Stock Exchange, was by far the best suitor for Phoenix.

The nature of the bidding for Phoenix has surprised Copenhagen's conservative business community where such deals are usually agreed quietly between the parties involved. --Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
